reason: The rover has one last invitation to deliver before the fair opens.
expectation: The rover will help welcome the guests before the flying show.

effect: The rover made a welcome banner rather than interacting directly with the fair; the banner is now ready to use.
reaction: The looping border and Kit’s hatted whale are a pleasing result, although I guessed the wrong partner.
reason: The finished welcome banner belongs at the fair entrance or display.
expectation: The banner will be displayed as part of welcoming the guests.

effect: The banner is hung on the grounded cradle, clear of the tether lines; the fair is ready for its controls.
reaction: The placement is satisfying and keeps the safety lines clear.
reason: The lift-control key seems like the next step toward opening the flying fair, though I’m guessing the order of the two controls.
expectation: The key will let Jo raise the tethered whale.

alternatives.reason: The attractions could perhaps be switched on before lifting.

effect: The lift-control key has no available operation yet, so the attractions likely need to be switched on first.
reaction: The ordering was not clear to me, but the failed attempt narrows the next choice.
reason: The accessory-switch key is the other control available for the bannered whale.
expectation: The dragon and star theatre will start before the lift.

effect: The dragon and star projector are running, so the lift control is the next plausible step.
reaction: Seeing both attractions work together is satisfying.
reason: The lift-control key was unavailable before the attractions started; now it may raise the whale.
expectation: Jo will be able to lift the tethered whale for the show.

effect: The lift control raised the tethered whale and completed the fair, bringing Jo’s drawing to life.
reaction: The dragon waving above the garden is a satisfying payoff to the preparations.

mostWorthwhile.text: Raising the whale was the most worthwhile moment: the moving dragon, projected stars and tethers came together in the finished show.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the lift key before the accessory switch was the least worthwhile moment; the required order was not clear to me.

surprise.text: The rover made the welcome banner rather than interacting directly with the fair, and Kit added a hatted whale.

arbitrary.text: The lift key being unavailable until the attractions were switched on felt somewhat arbitrary; I did not see a reason for that order.

continue.text: I would be curious to continue if another chapter offered a new mechanism to investigate. This finale was satisfying, though its main pleasure was seeing earlier constructions come together rather than learning how a new one worked.
